thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency > SLO on dedicated pool eu3-pool-13. Queue depth rising, streaming stalls reported. Paging oncall: @mira (oncall).

mira (oncall): I'm on it. seeing p95 ~1.1s but p99 jumping to ~4.2s on the eu3 dedicated pool, streaming sessions show partial frames then stalls. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/eu3-pool-13 (open).

sam (sre): FYI saw a spike in queue_depth metric on the pool's ingress queue: `queue_depth ~ 420` and enqueue rate spiked. Autoscaler logs show several failed warmup handshakes.

dario (runtime): past 30m we've seen autoscaler probe timeouts — handshake timeout = 30s, warmup pods not finishing readiness because KV-cache restore is slow for these checkpoints. I can tail the handshake logs.

li (platform): pulling autoscaler events... `Autoscaler: ScaleUp requested 6 -> 12 but WarmupTimeout for slot handshake for 80%` — looks like warmup_policy=conservative is still in effect for this pool.

support-ops: multiple customers reporting "responses hang" and streaming cutouts. ticket #C-11234 has SLA mention. Customer-visible errors ~0.6% of requests in last 10m.

mira (oncall): Action plan: 1) mitigate customer impact now (manual scale / fallback), 2) triage root cause (warmup/handshake), 3) page infra/runtime owners and consider runbook change. tagging @dario @li.

dario (runtime): I'll try a manual slot spawn to bypass autoscaler warmup gating. Command: 
```
# internal spawn CLI
redwoodctl pools spawn --pool eu3-pool-13 --count 4 --hotshot=true
```
Expect new slots to start w/o waiting for probe-based autoscaler backoff.

deploy-bot: Manual scale initiated by li (platform) — 4 slots requested.

li (platform): kicked manual scale, also flipping the warmup_policy to "hotshot" for a short window to accept faster but higher-cost warmups: 
```
redwoodctl pools update eu3-pool-13 --warmup-policy hotshot --warmup-timeout 45s
```
This should allow more aggressive slot handshakes.

sam (sre): Observing immediate effect: queue_depth dropping from 420 -> 120 over 90s. p99 is trending down to ~2.1s. Good. But streaming stalls persist for a subset of long-tail sessions.

dario (runtime): digging into logs for a stalled session: found repeated `kvcache restore slow-read` entries for model rwl-7b-qdq at time of handshake. Suspect disk jitter on the warmup host image.

support-ops: customer-impact note: converted errors to "degraded" status for customers impacted; outreach queued.

mira (oncall): short-term traffic engineering: can we divert 15% of eu3-pool-13 traffic to hosted-fallback region (hosted API tier) to reduce pressure? fallback model will be rwl-7b-compatible but with lower throughput guarantees.

li (platform): Yes. Pushing routing rule now: 
```
# feature flag / routing patch
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/router/update -d '{"pool":"eu3-pool-13","routeFallback":"eu-hosted-1","weight":0.15}'
```
Applied. Monitoring routing change.

(ops): routing change observed, traffic shifted ~14.8% in 2m. p99 on pool now ~1.6s, overall request errors drop to 0.12%.

sam (sre): still seeing streaming tail stalls ~0.3% of sessions. hypothesis: some KV checkpoints are large and cause cold restore stalls under disk IO pressure. dario, can we force smaller checkpoint loads on warmup?

dario (runtime): Forcing incremental kv prefetch helps, but that requires a runtime config flip. I'll toggle `kv_prefetch=incremental` for eu3-pool-13 temporarily: 
```
redwoodctl runtime set eu3-pool-13 --kv-prefetch incremental
```
Toggle in 30s.

deploy-bot: runtime config change applied by dario.

sam (sre): early telemetry: session stalls cut in half. p99 down to ~1.2s, streaming stall rate ~0.14%. Good.

mira (oncall): We're in recovery. Current mitigations: manual scale + hotshot warmup_policy + traffic diversion + kv_prefetch incremental. Owners: runtime(dario) + platform(li) + oncall(mira).

support-ops: Customer outreach: notified 6 affected accounts, offering detailed summary and ETA for postmortem.

mira (oncall): Next steps: 1) keep monitoring for 2h, 2) revert hotshot policy after pool stabilizes to avoid cost bleed, 3) prepare incident postmortem with timeline and runbook changes (autoscaler warmup_policy update and health probes), 4) run targeted warmup testing for large checkpoints. Please add any follow-ups.

dario (runtime): I'll collect handshake logs and PV IO metrics for the time window and create an artifact.

li (platform): I'll propose a policy change to have an emergency hotshot window and a fast-path for manual spawn that bypasses certain readiness checks for critical bursts. Will open RFC.

sam (sre): Add a monitoring alert refinement to detect queue_depth growth earlier (threshold lower) and to correlate with handshake-timeout counts.

mira (oncall): Thanks all. I'll close the paging but keep this thread open for follow-ups. Marking incident severity: SEV2 (customer-visible but mitigated).

incident-bot: Incident annotated: severity=SEV2, start=1765054321, mitigated=1765054480, owners=[mira (oncall), dario (runtime), li (platform)]. Please file postmortem within 72h. :white_check_mark:
